response.answer: Depthwise separable convolutions significantly reduce memory while preserving effectiveness. They split convolution into depthwise and pointwise layers. Lightweight alternatives like low-precision embeddings also help reduce memory.

results.title: Depthwise Separable Convolution - an overview | ScienceDirect Topics
results.content: Depthwise separable convolution is defined as a method in convolutional neural networks that minimizes computational complexity by splitting a standard convolution operation into two parts: depthwise convolution, which independently convolves each input channel with its own filters, and pointwise convolution, which combines the output channels. Inverted Linear Bottlenecks Inverted Linear Bottleneck block is designed for efficient neural network–based models, which employed the depthwise separable convolution to reduce the computational cost of the conventional convolution and further used more channels to improve the capability of feature extraction. Lightweight CNN-based methods Depthwise separable convolution is a convolutional operation used to reduce model parameters and computational complexity, marking the inception of lightweight network research. Various techniques, such as network pruning during architecture search , the construction of compact network blocks, the utilization of skip connections or residual connections , and the implementation of depthwise separable convolutions , have the potential to result in models that are more efficient in terms of parameters and processing resources.

results.content: # Depthwise separable Convolution. I am new to Deep Learning and I recently came across Depth Wise Separable Convolutions. Intuitively, depthwise separable conovolutions (DSCs) model the spatial correlation and cross-channel correlation separately while regular convolutions model them simultaneously. While regular convolutional layers will merge feature maps over the number of input channels, depthwise separable convolutions will perform another 1x1 convolution before adding them up. Using a depthwise separable convolutional layer as a drop-in replacement for a regular one will greatly reduce the number of weights in the model. At the same time a depthwise separable model with the same number of weights might achieve a higher accuracy compared the original model. I'm sure you will find use cases of depthwise separable models outside image related tasks. results.content: Efficient depthwise separable convolution accelerator for classification and UAV object detection. Depthwise separable convolutions (DSC) have been widely deployed in lightweight convolutional neural networks due to high efficiency. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have become the mainstream approach in the computational vision field [1], [2], [3], [4] because of their high accuracy. [23] exploited the inherent parallelism in CNNs to reduce the required bandwidth, resource usage, and power consumption of highly computationally complex convolution operations, and the proposed hardware accelerator only used 391 DSP48 and obtained 19.2 Giga multiply accumulation operations per second while consuming less than 10 watts (W) in power. However, most hardware accelerators were designed for large CNNs, which were not very suitable for depthwise separable convolution (DSC) because of the special operation and low MAC/FLOPs of the DWC. Then, spatial to channel (S2C), D2P&P2D, sharing processing element (SharePE) between DWC and pointwise convolution (PWC), regulable parallelism (R-Parallel) in computing unit, and pre-load workflow are proposed to improve the resource utilization rate, reduce the external memory access and speed up the accelerator. * •An efficient SharePE was proposed to compute depthwise separable convolution, which could compute efficiently DWC and PWC, and had a high computing resource utilization rate for DWC and PWC. * •A spatial to channel approach was proposed to accelerate the computing of preceding DWC layers in CNNs, which could improve the utilization rate of computational resources and bandwidth. Depthwise separable convolution has fewer parameters and computing costs than standard convolution, which is widely used in lightweight convolutional neural networks.
